summary: Backend-only iteration 20 verification completed against the public preview URL. Custom checklist create/merge/toggle/un-toggle/delete/completion cleanup, validation, and the sequential 20-item cap passed. Intake branding exposed firm name/logo/website before and after submission without signer PII. Extracted invite CRUD/public accept and both 2-way and 6-way atomic accept races passed. One intermittent concurrency defect was reproduced: 25 simultaneous custom-step creates admitted 21 items in the first run, although the retry admitted exactly 20. Requested billing, invite/auth/logo, non-provider bounce/profile, email-history, and billing-portal regressions passed; the known CORS wildcard assertion was excluded from success totals as requested.

critical.issue: The 20-step cap is non-atomic. One of two 25-request concurrency runs returned 21 successful creates and persisted more than the allowed maximum. The retry happened to return 20 successes and 5 HTTP 400 responses, confirming a race rather than a deterministic validation failure.

action_items: Make custom-step admission atomic in MongoDB: condition the update on the current custom_checklist_items array size being below 20 and return HTTP 400 when the conditional update does not match; then rerun the 25-request concurrency test repeatedly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1536-1548 checks len(existing) on the request's previously loaded user snapshot and performs an unconditional $push. Concurrent requests can all pass the stale length check before any push completes; use one conditional atomic update instead.

server.py remains 2,321 lines, well above the 700-line maintainability threshold. Invite extraction is registered correctly and its route suite passed, but renewal checklist and intake routes should continue moving into focused router modules.
routes/invites.py acceptance atomically claims used_at and passed six-way one-winner testing; CRUD/list wrapper/detail/public-info/delete behavior also remained intact after extraction.

success_rate.backend: 98% stable (56/57 relevant distinct tests passed without a product defect; the custom-limit concurrency case failed once and passed once). Billing 15/15, iteration 14 relevant tests 17/17, iteration 15 4/4, iteration 16 non-provider 6/6, and iteration 17-19 compatibility/portal checks 5/5 passed.

flaky_tests.classification: Product race confirmed by non-atomic read-then-push implementation

seed_data_creation: Created isolated checklist users, temporary branded admin intake, invite targets/accepted users/race users, billing users and Stripe test customers/sessions, lockout/logo/seal/profile/bounce/email-history resources. Mongo test resources and admin branding/profile state were restored or removed; immutable Stripe sandbox session history and attempted external invite-email activity remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run test_iteration20.py, especially the 25-way custom-create race, several times after the atomic limit fix. All sequential custom CRUD/validation/count/cleanup cases are green. Public intake branding and no-PII assertions are green. All invite tests in iteration 14/15 plus iteration 20 passed with the required {invites:[...]} wrapper and exactly one concurrent accept winner. test_iteration14.py was corrected from its obsolete list-shape assertion to the current wrapper contract. Its only failure was the explicitly excluded pre-existing CORS wildcard check. Do not run Resend-quota-dependent tests.
rca_of_the_issue: add_custom_checklist_item receives a user document before endpoint execution, computes existing = user.custom_checklist_items, rejects only when that stale snapshot already has 20 items, then issues an unconditional $push. Multiple requests that observe 19 or fewer items can all pass and push, exceeding 20. Reproduction: on a fresh user, issue 25 simultaneous POST /api/renewal-checklist/custom requests; the first run produced 21 HTTP 200 responses. Mitigation: combine the size predicate and push in a single atomic update and use matched/modified count to return the cap error.
